finding.expected: Deterministically distinguish non-target skipped source-workflow completions from target source completions before requiring a pointer. Non-target skipped runs must remain NO_WAKE, while a target source run that should have exported a selector but has a missing, malformed or substituted handoff must still produce only WAKE_SOURCE_HANDOFF_FAILURE. Add regressions reproducing the sibling-skipped workflow_run topology so one ordinary Issue event cannot generate false Brain attention.
finding.issue: The bridge treats every completed configured source workflow as if a wake-source artifact were expected. The existing Issue-triggered ingress/PRIMARY/REPAIR workflows are repository-wide triggers with title-gated jobs, so one logical Issue event also creates non-target workflow runs whose jobs conclude skipped and intentionally produce no source pointer. consume_handoff enters the source handoff path for those skipped runs, fails to find the artifact, and projects WAKE_SOURCE_HANDOFF_FAILURE. Therefore ordinary non-target bookkeeping can wake Brain even though no semantic decision is required. This topology is already visible in the TASK-255 deliveries themselves: sibling source workflows for a [AIOS BRAIN WAKEUP] Issue complete as skipped.
